claims.text: Rapid consolidation such as spark plasma sintering produces a non-equilibrium, homogeneous, single-phase metastable solid solution containing Mg.
The as-sintered target alloy has high inherent corrosion resistance.
The as-sintered target alloy has high inherent oxidation resistance.
Aging at 400–500 °C causes nucleation and growth of fine Mg-rich intermetallic phases from the metastable solid solution.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates form preferentially along grain boundaries.
Increasing thermal exposure increases atomic mobility and elemental diffusion.
Increased atomic mobility drives separation of the metastable solid solution into equilibrium phases.
The emerging intermetallic phases interrupt the structural continuity of the alloy.
Intermetallic precipitates provide preferential transport paths for oxygen and aggressive ions.
Intermetallic precipitation undermines the integrity or continuity of the initially protective oxide or passive layer.
The precipitation-mediated loss of film integrity accelerates aqueous corrosion.
The precipitation-mediated loss of film integrity accelerates high-temperature oxidation.
Thermally aged samples will contain a detectably greater intermetallic precipitate population than the initial homogeneous state.
Thermally aged samples will have a higher oxidation mass gain than unaged controls.
Thermally aged samples will have a higher corrosion current density than unaged controls.
The 400–500 °C service range is sufficient to activate diffusion in the target alloy.
Keeping exposure below approximately 600 °C avoids dramatic grain coarsening.
Below approximately 300 °C, intermetallic precipitation is negligible because diffusion is limited.
Exposure in an inert atmosphere limits the transformation and preserves oxide or passive-film integrity.
Reported Mg-containing multi-principal-element alloys have a tendency to develop multiple or intermetallic phases, including Laves phases.

contradictions.description: The stated service regime is bounded below approximately 600 °C to avoid dramatic coarsening, but oxidation performance is evaluated at 900 °C without explaining why this out-of-regime test preserves relevance to the proposed service mechanism.
